rules.exact_quote: No bail shall be granted to a criminal suspect or defendant unless the judge has sufficient grounds for believing that the criminal suspect or defendant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security.
rules.proposition_text: NSL Article 42(2) sets a no-bail-unless threshold for national security bail applications.
rules.lineage_note: CFA statement of the statutory text used in construing NSL Article 42(2).

rules.exact_quote: Plainly, NSL 42(2) introduces a considerably more stringent threshold requirement.
rules.proposition_text: For NSL bail, Article 42(2) introduces a threshold materially more stringent than ordinary bail under the Criminal Procedure Ordinance.
rules.lineage_note: CFA distinguishes the NSL Article 42 threshold from ordinary bail.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) operates in the context or matrix of the existing bail regime and draws on its rules and principles insofar as they may be relevant, while introducing a new and more stringent threshold requirement for the grant of bail.
rules.proposition_text: NSL Article 42(2) operates as a specific exception within the existing bail regime, rather than replacing the whole bail regime.
rules.lineage_note: CFA frames NSL Article 42(2) as a special threshold within the wider bail system.

rules.exact_quote: it makes no sense presumptively to exclude bail conditions from consideration.
rules.proposition_text: When assessing NSL Article 42(2), the court may consider whether bail conditions affect the future risk assessment.
rules.lineage_note: CFA rejects a sealed-off first stage that excludes proposed bail conditions.

rules.exact_quote: The imposition of appropriate conditions therefore possesses a deterrent value that may plainly be relevant to the risk assessment.
rules.proposition_text: Appropriate bail conditions may be relevant to the risk assessment because they can deter breach or further offending.
rules.lineage_note: CFA connects conditions to risk management and deterrence.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) creates a specific exception to the HKSAR rules and principles governing the grant and refusal of bail, and imports a stringent threshold requirement for bail applications.
rules.proposition_text: The CFA summarised NSL Article 42(2) as a specific exception importing a stringent threshold for bail.
rules.lineage_note: CFA summary of conclusions.

rules.exact_quote: that judgment unfortunately falls into error and is flawed in a crucial respect in that it misapprehends the nature and effect of the threshold requirement laid down by NSL 42(2).
rules.proposition_text: The CFA held that Tong (No 1) erred in a crucial respect by misapprehending the nature and effect of the NSL Article 42(2) threshold.
rules.lineage_note: Lineage marker showing Lai limiting/correcting Tong on NSL bail threshold.

rules.exact_quote: Article 42(2), in substance, targets such risk in respect of offences endangering national security.
rules.proposition_text: Tong treated Article 42(2) as targeting the risk of offending while on bail in respect of national security offences.
rules.lineage_note: Earlier CFI treatment; must be read with later CFA correction in Lai Chee Ying.

rules.exact_quote: the effect of Article 42 is to emphasize the particular weight which the bail court ought to give to the “risk of re-offending” when dealing with offences under the NSL.
rules.proposition_text: Tong treated NSL Article 42 as emphasizing the weight to be given to risk of reoffending in NSL bail applications.
rules.lineage_note: Earlier CFI application on Article 42 risk weighting; answer composers must show later CFA treatment in Lai Chee Ying.

rules.exact_quote: Article 42 does not shut out the accused from making a bail application.
rules.proposition_text: Tong stated that Article 42 does not wholly shut out a defendant from applying for bail.
rules.lineage_note: Earlier CFI statement; read with the CFA's later framing of Article 42 as a stringent threshold.

rules.exact_quote: The judge has to form a view on what the accused person may or may not do in the future.
rules.proposition_text: In NSL bail review, the court's future-risk assessment is a judgment on what the accused may or may not do in the future.
rules.lineage_note: Useful candidate paragraph on the predictive nature of bail risk assessment.

rules.exact_quote: bail should be refused on either one of the two aforesaid conventional grounds, namely the “flight risk” and the “risk of re-offending”
rules.proposition_text: Tong refused bail on conventional grounds of flight risk and risk of reoffending.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal illustration; not answer-safe without review.

rules.exact_quote: This court would not eliminate the giving of a similar undertaking as a means to satisfy the requirement of NSL 42(2) [38] for the granting of bail in an appropriate case.
rules.proposition_text: Ma treated an undertaking as a possible means, in an appropriate case, of satisfying the NSL Article 42(2) bail requirement.
rules.lineage_note: CFI candidate application on undertakings; must be compared with factual refusal at paragraph 33 and later CFA treatment.

rules.exact_quote: it is difficult for this court to accept that the Applicant would abide by his undertaking.
rules.proposition_text: Ma illustrates that a proposed undertaking may fail to satisfy the bail court where the facts suggest the defendant may not abide by it.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive refusal despite proposed undertaking; useful as contrast to Lai CFI paragraph 33.

rules.exact_quote: it may eventually come to a stage when it could be unjust to detain the Applicant any longer before trial.
rules.proposition_text: Ma recognises that prolonged pre-trial detention may eventually justify a renewed bail review depending on the later state of affairs.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate point on renewed review/new circumstances; not a general entitlement without factual review.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) is not a “no-bail” provision.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI in Lai treated NSL Article 42(2) as not being a categorical no-bail provision.
rules.lineage_note: CFI statement later considered by the CFA in the same litigation; show with CFA Article 42 threshold propositions.

rules.exact_quote: I am satisfied that the above undertaking which is tailor-made to the present case, coupled with the Applicant’s agreement to be confined to his residence during the whole of the bail period, give this court sufficient grounds to believe that the accused will not commit acts endangering national security for the future if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI in Lai accepted a case-specific undertaking and residence confinement as sufficient on the facts before it for the Article 42 future-risk assessment.
rules.lineage_note: CFI bail-grant illustration later reviewed in CFA proceedings; candidate lineage only.

rules.exact_quote: A decision to refuse or grant bail is not final. Bail granted can be revoked. The decision to refuse bail can be reopened on new circumstances being shown.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI in Lai stated that bail decisions are not final: bail can be revoked and refusal can be reopened on new circumstances.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate procedural point on bail review/revocation/new circumstances.

rules.exact_quote: No bail shall be granted to a criminal suspect or defendant unless the judge has sufficient grounds for believing that the criminal suspect or defendant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security.
rules.proposition_text: The post-CFA Lai bail review restated the NSL Article 42(2) no-bail-unless formulation.
rules.lineage_note: CFI post-CFA restatement of Article 42(2); pair with CFA ratio propositions for answer hierarchy.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) creates a specific exception to the HKSAR rules and principles governing the grant and refusal of bail, and imports a stringent threshold requirement for bail applications.
rules.proposition_text: The post-CFA Lai bail review applied the CFA's formulation that NSL Article 42(2) imports a stringent threshold for bail.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of the CFA Article 42 threshold; CFA remains the controlling source.

rules.exact_quote: the judge should consider everything that appears to the court to be relevant to making that decision, including the possible imposition of appropriate bail conditions and materials which would not be admissible as evidence at the trial
rules.proposition_text: In applying the Article 42(2) threshold, the bail court may consider all apparently relevant materials, including proposed conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
rules.lineage_note: CFI post-CFA application of the factors/materials part of the Article 42 assessment.

rules.exact_quote: all bail decisions “involve a risk assessment looking to the future”.
rules.proposition_text: The post-CFA Lai bail review emphasised that bail decisions involve a future-looking risk assessment.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate application point on forward-looking bail risk assessment.

rules.exact_quote: the question is not only about the alleged commission of the NSL 29(4) acts but any of the prohibited acts.
rules.proposition_text: The Article 42(2) future-risk inquiry is not confined to repeating the charged conduct, but may extend to prohibited acts more broadly.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI application on scope of prohibited acts in future-risk assessment.

rules.exact_quote: I am not satisfied that there are sufficient grounds for believing that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted to him.
rules.proposition_text: The post-CFA Lai bail review refused bail because the court was not satisfied that the Article 42(2) future-risk threshold was met.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal after applying the CFA Article 42 framework.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) creates a specific exception to the HKSAR rules and principles governing the grant and refusal of bail, and imports a stringent threshold requirement for bail applications.
rules.proposition_text: Chan applied the CFA formulation that NSL Article 42(2) imports a stringent threshold for bail applications.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of Lai CFA threshold in a later NSL bail review.

rules.exact_quote: the “judge should consider everything that appears to the court to be relevant to making that decision including the possible imposition of appropriate bail conditions and materials which would not be admissible as evidence at the trial”.
rules.proposition_text: Chan applied the Article 42(2) approach that the bail court considers all relevant matters, including proposed conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
rules.lineage_note: CFI candidate application of the CFA factor/materials approach.

rules.exact_quote: the court in considering bail, has to look at the individual circumstances of each particular applicant.
rules.proposition_text: Chan illustrates that NSL bail assessment remains applicant-specific and requires consideration of the individual's circumstances.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate application point on individualised bail assessment.

rules.exact_quote: everything including matters of public record and assertions, which may not be of public record, including the applicant’s past performance, and conduct, and the bail conditions offered
rules.proposition_text: Chan treated public-record matters, non-public assertions, past performance, conduct, and offered bail conditions as relevant to the predictive assessment.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate illustration of facts considered in the predictive and evaluative exercise.

rules.exact_quote: with the conditions imposed for bail that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: Chan illustrates a case where conditions were treated as sufficient on the facts to satisfy the Article 42(2) future-risk threshold.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive grant illustration; not a general rule without review.

rules.exact_quote: with the stringent bail conditions imposed, that the Applicant will surrender to custody at the appointed time.
rules.proposition_text: Chan illustrates that stringent conditions may address surrender-to-custody risk on the facts of a bail review.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive ordinary bail-risk illustration within NSL bail review.

rules.exact_quote: failed to overcome the first threshold of the test laid down by the CFA in the case of HKSAR v Lai Chee Ying
rules.proposition_text: Fan frames the NSL bail inquiry as requiring the applicant to overcome the first threshold laid down in Lai CFA.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate second-bail-application source using Lai CFA threshold terminology.

rules.exact_quote: I am however, concerned about the long delay in the proceeding being brought to trial.
rules.proposition_text: Fan treats long delay before trial as a relevant concern in a second NSL bail application, although not automatically decisive.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate delay/new-circumstances point for second bail applications.

rules.exact_quote: There should be proactive case management and a monitoring of progress by the court rather than leaving all initiatives to the parties while the person remanded remains in pre-trial custody for lengthy periods.
rules.proposition_text: Fan cites the need for proactive case management where a remanded NSL defendant remains in pre-trial custody for lengthy periods.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate pre-trial delay/case-management point; source quotes Ng Hau Yi Sidney through Fan.

rules.exact_quote: the long wait for committal and possibly trial, which as she said, militates against fairness to her client.
rules.proposition_text: Fan records that long wait for committal and trial may be raised as a fairness concern in a renewed bail application.
rules.lineage_note: Candidate fairness/delay point; paragraph records submission and must be labelled carefully until reviewed.

rules.exact_quote: the Applicant has not managed to overcome the first threshold.
rules.proposition_text: Fan refused the second bail application because the applicant still had not overcome the first Article 42/Lai threshold.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive refusal on a second application; not a general rule.

rules.exact_quote: NSL 42(2) creates a specific exception to the HKSAR rules and principles governing the grant and refusal of bail, and imports a stringent threshold requirement for bail applications.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI applied Lai CFA as establishing that NSL Article 42(2) is a stringent threshold exception to ordinary bail principles.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of Lai CFA threshold; candidate only and subordinate to CFA ratio.

rules.exact_quote: the terms and bail conditions as imposed by the learned Chief Magistrate would be sufficient to ensure that the Respondent will surrender himself to custody as the Court may appoint.
rules.proposition_text: Bail conditions may satisfy the ordinary second-threshold concern of surrendering to custody.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI application on surrender-risk conditions.

rules.exact_quote: consider everything that appears to the court to be relevant to making that decision including the possible imposition of appropriate bail conditions and materials which would not be admissible as evidence at the trial
rules.proposition_text: In NSL bail applications, the CFI applied Lai CFA as permitting consideration of all relevant matters, including bail conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of the CFA all-relevant-materials approach.

rules.exact_quote: on making my predictive assessment and evaluation, there are insufficient grounds for believing that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: A predictive and evaluative assessment may lead to refusal where there are insufficient grounds to believe the applicant will not continue acts endangering national security.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal applying the NSL bail threshold.

rules.exact_quote: I have to make a “predictive and evaluative” exercise at this stage, of all the materials before me, whether the Court has sufficient grounds for believing that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI characterised NSL bail assessment as a predictive and evaluative exercise on all materials before the court.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of predictive/evaluative assessment terminology.

rules.exact_quote: I do not have sufficient grounds for believing that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: On the facts, absence of sufficient grounds under the NSL threshold led to refusal of bail.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal; candidate only.

rules.exact_quote: after performing my “predictive and evaluative” exercise, on the materials before me, and counsel’s submissions, both written and oral, and the bail conditions offered, I consider that there are insufficient grounds for believing that the Applicant will not continue to commit acts endangering national security if bail is granted.
rules.proposition_text: The CFI considered materials, submissions and proposed bail conditions in a predictive and evaluative NSL bail assessment, but refused bail where sufficient grounds were absent.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal after considering proposed conditions.

rules.exact_quote: the judge should consider everything that appears to the court to be relevant to making that decision, including the possible imposition of appropriate bail conditions and materials which would not be admissible as evidence at the trial
rules.proposition_text: The CFI applied Lai CFA by considering all relevant matters, including possible bail conditions and materials not admissible at trial.
rules.lineage_note: CFI application of CFA all-relevant-materials approach.

rules.exact_quote: with the conditions that I have imposed for bail, that he will not continue to commit any offences under the NSL if bail is granted to him.
rules.proposition_text: On the facts, imposed bail conditions satisfied the court that the applicant would not continue NSL offences if granted bail.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI grant illustration; not a general rule without review.

rules.exact_quote: whether the Applicant would fail to surrender to custody or commit an offence while on bail, I am satisfied that with the conditions I have imposed he would not do so.
rules.proposition_text: Bail conditions may satisfy ordinary s.9G concerns about surrendering to custody or committing an offence while on bail.
rules.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI grant illustration on ordinary second threshold.
